cover letter
Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience and/or training.
Experience coordinating multiple programs and events simultaneously, including logistics, timelines, and participant communications.
Experience providing administrative support in a higher education setting.
Knowledge of budget, accounting, and purchasing processes, including experience with procurement or expense reimbursement.
Experience with project management software or tools.
Experience creating print and digital materials using design tools such as Canva or Adobe InDesign.
Experience providing calendar and administrative support to senior leaders.

The Teaching and Learning Center (TLC) Program Coordinator is an experienced administrative operations professional who provides administrative and operational support for all TLC programs, services, and events, as well as for center operations. The TLC Program Coordinator reports to the TLC Managing Director and supports programming across every TLC program area, including faculty development, graduate student and postdoctoral professional development, instructional design and media, and accessibility and instructional technology. This includes support for all staff who lead programs, workshops, learning communities, and other services. The Program Coordinator also provides administrative support to TLC executive leadership.

The position requires that the incumbent exercise discretion and independent judgment. The TLC Program Coordinator must be able to excel while working in a fast-paced environment with a wide range of staff and campus partners and often competing short- and long-term deadlines, and to prioritize requests across multiple programs. The TLC Program Coordinator is expected to determine methods and procedures on new assignments, and to leverage technology in ways that are aligned with TLC guidelines to create workplace efficiencies.
Orientation toward excellence in customer service.
Selected candidate will be required to pass a pre-employment criminal history background check.
Selected candidate must pass the employment misconduct disclosure process.

The selected candidate will be required to work primarily on campus, with periods of remote work possible based on operational needs. If a hybrid work schedule is confirmed, the selected candidate must be able to work successfully from a home/remote office and be able to fulfill the requirements of the UCSC telecommuting agreement.
Must reside within the State of California.
Selected candidate will be required to complete training within established time frames as directed including UC compliance training.

The University of California has implemented a Vaccination Policy covering all employees. Employees, including new hires, are required to comply with any applicable policies relating to the University of California vaccine program.

Per the Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act (CANRA), this position has been identified as a Mandated Reporter. The selected candidate will be required to report known or suspected child abuse or neglect as defined by CANRA and will be required to sign a Statement Acknowledging Requirement to Report Child Abuse prior to commencing employment. CANRA Penal Codes, and related definitions, requirements, and responsibilities may be obtained here.

Exercise the utmost discretion in managing sensitive information learned in the course of performing their duties. Sensitive information includes but is not limited to employee and student records, health and patient records, financial data, strategic plans, proprietary information and any other sensitive or non-public information learned during the course and scope of employment. Understands that sensitive information should be shared on a limited basis and actively takes steps to limit access to sensitive information to individuals who have legitimate business need to know. Ensure that sensitive information is properly safeguarded. Follow all organizational policies and laws on data protection and privacy. This includes secure handling of physical and digital records and proper usage of IT systems to prevent data leaks. The unauthorized or improper disclosure of confidential work-related information obtained from any source on any work-related matter is a violation of these expectations.
Organizational skills and the ability to prioritize requests from multiple staff with competing deadlines.
Knowledge of University rules, regulations, and procedures for budget, purchasing, and personnel.
Ability to work long periods of time at a computer with or without accommodation.
Solid knowledge of standard computing tools, including Google workspace and online databases with the ability to learn new systems quickly.
Knowledge of UCSC systems, such as CruzPay, CruzBuy, and the student hiring systems.
This position requires the ability to report to campus to work in-person as operationally required, with reasonable notice as determined by your manager; travel expenses not covered.
Verbal communication skills with a diversity of communication styles and the ability to listen effectively.
Knowledge of web content management systems, especially WordPress.
Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends as directed.
Interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively with all levels of the organization and external constituencies.
Ability to travel to multiple work locations on and off campus.
Effective written communication skills.
Critical thinking and problem solving skills.
Ability to act with discretion and use good judgment.
